  | mul {n} (i j : Fin n) : @ArithPart₁ n (fun v => v.get i * v.get j : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ)
  | proj {n} (i : Fin n) : @ArithPart₁ n (fun v => v.get i : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ)
  | equal {n} (i j : Fin n) : @ArithPart₁ n (fun v => isEqNat (v.get i) (v.get j) : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ)
  | lt {n} (i j : Fin n) : @ArithPart₁ n (fun v => isLtNat (v.get i) (v.get j) : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ)
  | comp {m n f} (g : Fin n → List.Vector ℕ m →. ℕ) :
    ArithPart₁ f → (∀ i, ArithPart₁ (g i)) → ArithPart₁ fun v => (List.Vector.mOfFn fun i => g i v) >>= f
  | rfind {n} {f : List.Vector ℕ (n + 1) → ℕ} :
    ArithPart₁ (n := n + 1) f → ArithPart₁ (fun v => rfind fun n => Part.some (f (n ::ᵥ v) = 0))

lemma to_partrec' {n} {f : List.Vector ℕ n →. ℕ} (hf : ArithPart₁ f) : Partrec' f := by
  induction hf
  case zero => exact Partrec'.of_part (Partrec.const' 0)
  case one  => exact Partrec'.of_part (Partrec.const' 1)
  case add n i j =>
    exact (Partrec'.of_part ((Primrec.nat_add.comp
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j))).to_comp.partrec))
  case mul n i j =>
    exact (Partrec'.of_part ((Primrec.nat_mul.comp
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j))).to_comp.partrec))
  case proj n i =>
    exact Partrec'.of_part
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i)).to_comp.partrec
  case equal n i j =>
    have : Primrec (fun (v : List.Vector ℕ n) => if v.get i = v.get j then 1 else 0) :=
      Primrec.ite
        (Primrec.eq.comp
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j)))
        (_root_.Primrec.const 1)
        (_root_.Primrec.const 0)
    exact Partrec'.of_part this.to_comp.partrec
  case lt n i j =>
    have : Primrec (fun (v : List.Vector ℕ n) => if v.get i < v.get j then 1 else 0) :=
      Primrec.ite
        (Primrec.nat_lt.comp
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j)))
        (_root_.Primrec.const 1)
        (_root_.Primrec.const 0)
    exact Partrec'.of_part this.to_comp.partrec
  case comp m n f g _ _ hf hg =>
    exact Partrec'.comp g hf hg

    exact Partrec'.rfind hf

lemma pos_of_eq_one (h : n = 1) : 0 < n := by simp[h]

def isEqNat (n m : ℕ) : ℕ := if n = m then 1 else 0

def isLtNat (n m : ℕ) : ℕ := if n < m then 1 else 0

def isLeNat (n m : ℕ) : ℕ := if n ≤ m then 1 else 0

def isDvdNat (n m : ℕ) : ℕ := if n ∣ m then 1 else 0

@[simp] lemma isEqNat_pos_iff : 0 < isEqNat n m ↔ n = m := by simp[isEqNat]; by_cases n = m <;> simp[*]

@[simp] lemma isLtNat_pos_iff : 0 < isLtNat n m ↔ n < m := by simp[isLtNat]; by_cases n < m <;> simp[*]

@[simp] lemma isLeNat_pos_iff : 0 < isLeNat n m ↔ n ≤ m := by simp[isLeNat]; by_cases n ≤ m <;> simp[*]

@[simp] lemma isDvdNat_pos_iff : 0 < isDvdNat n m ↔ n ∣ m := by simp[isDvdNat]; by_cases n ∣ m <;> simp[*]

def inv (n : ℕ) : ℕ := isEqNat n 0

def pos (n : ℕ) : ℕ := isLtNat 0 n

@[simp] lemma inv_zero : inv 0 = 1 := rfl

@[simp] lemma inv_iff_ne_zero : inv n = 0 ↔ 0 < n := by simp[inv, isEqNat, zero_lt_iff]

@[simp] lemma inv_ne_zero (h : n ≠ 0) : inv n = 0 := by simp[inv, isEqNat, h]

@[simp] lemma pos_zero : pos 0 = 0 := rfl

@[simp] lemma pos_ne_zero (h : n ≠ 0) : pos n = 1 := by simp[pos, isLtNat, h]

def and (n m : ℕ) : ℕ := isLtNat 0 (n * m)

def or (n m : ℕ) : ℕ := isLtNat 0 (n + m)

lemma and_eq (n m : ℕ) : and n m = if 0 < n ∧ 0 < m then 1 else 0 := by simp [mul_pos_iff, and, isLtNat]

lemma and_eq_one (n m : ℕ) : and n m = 1 ↔ 0 < n ∧ 0 < m := by simp[and_eq, imp_false, Nat.pos_iff_ne_zero]

lemma or_eq (n m : ℕ) : or n m = if 0 < n ∨ 0 < m then 1 else 0 := by simp[or, isLtNat]

@[simp] lemma and_pos_iff (n m : ℕ) : 0 < and n m ↔ 0 < n ∧ 0 < m := by simp[and_eq]; by_cases 0 < n ∧ 0 < m <;> simp[*]

@[simp] lemma or_pos_iff (n m : ℕ) : 0 < or n m ↔ 0 < n ∨ 0 < m := by simp[or_eq]; by_cases 0 < n ∨ 0 < m <;> simp[*]

@[simp] lemma inv_pos_iff (n : ℕ) : 0 < inv n ↔ ¬0 < n := by simp[inv]

@[simp] lemma pos_pos_iff (n : ℕ) : 0 < pos n ↔ 0 < n := by simp[pos]

def ball (n : ℕ) (φ : ℕ → ℕ) : ℕ := n.rec 1 (fun n ih => (φ n).pos.and ih)

@[simp] lemma ball_pos_iff {φ : ℕ → ℕ} {n : ℕ} : 0 < ball n φ ↔ ∀ m < n, 0 < φ m := by
  induction' n with n ih <;> simp[ball, Nat.lt_succ_iff] at*
  · simp[ih]; exact ⟨
    by rintro ⟨hn, hp⟩ m hm; rcases lt_or_eq_of_le hm with (hm | rfl); { exact hp _ hm }; { exact hn },
    by intro h; exact ⟨h n (Nat.le_refl n), fun m hm => h m (le_of_lt hm)⟩⟩

@[simp] lemma ball_eq_zero_iff {φ : ℕ → ℕ} {n : ℕ} : ball n φ = 0 ↔ ∃ m < n, φ m = 0 := by
  simpa[-ball_pos_iff] using not_iff_not.mpr (ball_pos_iff (φ := φ) (n := n))

lemma ball_pos_iff_eq_one {φ : ℕ → ℕ} {n : ℕ} : ball n φ = 1 ↔ 0 < ball n φ := by
  induction' n with n _ <;> simp[ball, Nat.lt_succ_iff] at*
  · constructor
    · intro h; simpa using pos_of_eq_one h
    · intro h; simpa[and_eq_one] using h

inductive ArithPart₁ : ∀ {n}, (List.Vector ℕ n →. ℕ) → Prop
  | zero {n} : @ArithPart₁ n (fun _ => 0)
  | one {n} : @ArithPart₁ n (fun _ => 1)
  | add {n} (i j : Fin n) : @ArithPart₁ n (fun v => v.get i + v.get j : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ)
  | mul {n} (i j : Fin n) : @ArithPart₁ n (fun v => v.get i * v.get j : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ)
  | proj {n} (i : Fin n) : @ArithPart₁ n (fun v => v.get i : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ)
  | equal {n} (i j : Fin n) : @ArithPart₁ n (fun v => isEqNat (v.get i) (v.get j) : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ)
  | lt {n} (i j : Fin n) : @ArithPart₁ n (fun v => isLtNat (v.get i) (v.get j) : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ)
  | comp {m n f} (g : Fin n → List.Vector ℕ m →. ℕ) :
    ArithPart₁ f → (∀ i, ArithPart₁ (g i)) → ArithPart₁ fun v => (List.Vector.mOfFn fun i => g i v) >>= f
  | rfind {n} {f : List.Vector ℕ (n + 1) → ℕ} :
    ArithPart₁ (n := n + 1) f → ArithPart₁ (fun v => rfind fun n => Part.some (f (n ::ᵥ v) = 0))

def Arith₁ (f : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ) := ArithPart₁ (n := n) f

end Nat

open Primrec

lemma to_partrec' {n} {f : List.Vector ℕ n →. ℕ} (hf : ArithPart₁ f) : Partrec' f := by
  induction hf
  case zero => exact Partrec'.of_part (Partrec.const' 0)
  case one  => exact Partrec'.of_part (Partrec.const' 1)
  case add n i j =>
    exact (Partrec'.of_part ((Primrec.nat_add.comp
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j))).to_comp.partrec))
  case mul n i j =>
    exact (Partrec'.of_part ((Primrec.nat_mul.comp
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j))).to_comp.partrec))
  case proj n i =>
    exact Partrec'.of_part
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i)).to_comp.partrec
  case equal n i j =>
    have : Primrec (fun (v : List.Vector ℕ n) => if v.get i = v.get j then 1 else 0) :=
      Primrec.ite
        (Primrec.eq.comp
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j)))
        (_root_.Primrec.const 1)
        (_root_.Primrec.const 0)
    exact Partrec'.of_part this.to_comp.partrec
  case lt n i j =>
    have : Primrec (fun (v : List.Vector ℕ n) => if v.get i < v.get j then 1 else 0) :=
      Primrec.ite
        (Primrec.nat_lt.comp
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j)))
        (_root_.Primrec.const 1)
        (_root_.Primrec.const 0)
    exact Partrec'.of_part this.to_comp.partrec
  case comp m n f g _ _ hf hg =>
    exact Partrec'.comp g hf hg
  case rfind f _ hf =>
    exact Partrec'.rfind hf

        rw[←List.Vector.mOfFn_pure]; apply congr_arg
        funext i; cases i using Fin.cases <;> simp[hgv]
      simp[this])

lemma to_partrec' {n} {f : List.Vector ℕ n →. ℕ} (hf : ArithPart₁ f) : Partrec' f := by
  induction hf
  case zero => exact Partrec'.of_part (Partrec.const' 0)
  case one  => exact Partrec'.of_part (Partrec.const' 1)
  case add n i j =>
    exact (Partrec'.of_part ((Primrec.nat_add.comp
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j))).to_comp.partrec))
  case mul n i j =>
    exact (Partrec'.of_part ((Primrec.nat_mul.comp
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j))).to_comp.partrec))
  case proj n i =>
    exact Partrec'.of_part
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i)).to_comp.partrec
  case equal n i j =>
    have : Primrec (fun (v : List.Vector ℕ n) => if v.get i = v.get j then 1 else 0) :=
      Primrec.ite
        (Primrec.eq.comp
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j)))
        (_root_.Primrec.const 1)
        (_root_.Primrec.const 0)
    exact Partrec'.of_part this.to_comp.partrec
  case lt n i j =>
    have : Primrec (fun (v : List.Vector ℕ n) => if v.get i < v.get j then 1 else 0) :=
      Primrec.ite
        (Primrec.nat_lt.comp
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j)))
        (_root_.Primrec.const 1)
        (_root_.Primrec.const 0)
    exact Partrec'.of_part this.to_comp.partrec
  case comp m n f g _ _ hf hg =>
    exact Partrec'.comp g hf hg
  case rfind f _ hf =>
    exact Partrec'.rfind hf

informal_statement: Function composition is associative. Specifically, for any functions \( f: A \to B \) and \( g: C \to A \), the composition \( f \circ g \) is the same as the composition of \( f \) after \( g \), demonstrating that function composition follows the associative property.
informal_proof:
To understand why function composition is associative, let's break it down step by step.

1. **Understanding Function Composition**: Function composition involves applying one function to the results of another. If we have two functions \( f: A \to B \) and \( g: C \to A \), then the composition \( f \circ g \) is defined as \( f(g(c)) \) for any element \( c \) in the domain \( C \).

2. **Defining Associativity**: The associativity property states that the order of composition does not affect the outcome. In mathematical terms, for any three functions \( f \), \( g \), and \( h \) where the compositions are defined, the equation \( f \circ (g \circ h) = (f \circ g) \circ h \) must hold true.

3. **Applying to the Given Lemma**: In our specific case, we have the lemma `comp₁` which focuses on two functions, \( f \) and \( g \), and demonstrates that their composition follows the associative property.

   - The tactic `constructor` splits the proof into multiple parts, addressing each direction of the equivalence separately.
   - The tactic `intro` inside `constructor` is used to introduce the variable \( h \), which represents the result of the composition \( hg \).
   - The tactic `exact` is used to provide a direct proof by applying previously known properties (`simp`) to simplify the expression and establish the equality between \( f \circ (g \circ h) \) and \( (f \circ g) \circ h \).

5. **Simplifying the Explanation**:
   - The above steps are essentially showing that when you compose three functions, the way you group them does not change the final result. This is what associativity means.

6. **Concluding the Proof**: By following the steps indicated by the Lean4 tactics, we have demonstrated that function composition inherently follows the associative property.

lemma pos_of_eq_one (h : n = 1) : 0 < n := by simp[h]

def isEqNat (n m : ℕ) : ℕ := if n = m then 1 else 0

def isLtNat (n m : ℕ) : ℕ := if n < m then 1 else 0

def isLeNat (n m : ℕ) : ℕ := if n ≤ m then 1 else 0

def isDvdNat (n m : ℕ) : ℕ := if n ∣ m then 1 else 0

@[simp] lemma isEqNat_pos_iff : 0 < isEqNat n m ↔ n = m := by simp[isEqNat]; by_cases n = m <;> simp[*]

@[simp] lemma isLtNat_pos_iff : 0 < isLtNat n m ↔ n < m := by simp[isLtNat]; by_cases n < m <;> simp[*]

@[simp] lemma isLeNat_pos_iff : 0 < isLeNat n m ↔ n ≤ m := by simp[isLeNat]; by_cases n ≤ m <;> simp[*]

def inv (n : ℕ) : ℕ := isEqNat n 0

def pos (n : ℕ) : ℕ := isLtNat 0 n

@[simp] lemma pos_zero : pos 0 = 0 := rfl

def and (n m : ℕ) : ℕ := isLtNat 0 (n * m)

def or (n m : ℕ) : ℕ := isLtNat 0 (n + m)

lemma and_eq (n m : ℕ) : and n m = if 0 < n ∧ 0 < m then 1 else 0 := by simp [mul_pos_iff, and, isLtNat]

lemma and_eq_one (n m : ℕ) : and n m = 1 ↔ 0 < n ∧ 0 < m := by simp[and_eq, imp_false, Nat.pos_iff_ne_zero]

lemma or_eq (n m : ℕ) : or n m = if 0 < n ∨ 0 < m then 1 else 0 := by simp[or, isLtNat]

@[simp] lemma and_pos_iff (n m : ℕ) : 0 < and n m ↔ 0 < n ∧ 0 < m := by simp[and_eq]; by_cases 0 < n ∧ 0 < m <;> simp[*]

def ball (n : ℕ) (φ : ℕ → ℕ) : ℕ := n.rec 1 (fun n ih => (φ n).pos.and ih)

@[simp] lemma ball_pos_iff {φ : ℕ → ℕ} {n : ℕ} : 0 < ball n φ ↔ ∀ m < n, 0 < φ m := by
  induction' n with n ih <;> simp[ball, Nat.lt_succ_iff] at*

@[simp] lemma isLtNat_pos_iff : 0 < isLtNat n m ↔ n < m := by simp[isLtNat]; by_cases n < m <;> simp[*]

@[simp] lemma isLeNat_pos_iff : 0 < isLeNat n m ↔ n ≤ m := by simp[isLeNat]; by_cases n ≤ m <;> simp[*]

def inv (n : ℕ) : ℕ := isEqNat n 0

def pos (n : ℕ) : ℕ := isLtNat 0 n

lemma and_eq (n m : ℕ) : and n m = if 0 < n ∧ 0 < m then 1 else 0 := by simp [mul_pos_iff, and, isLtNat]

lemma or_eq (n m : ℕ) : or n m = if 0 < n ∨ 0 < m then 1 else 0 := by simp[or, isLtNat]

@[simp] lemma and_pos_iff (n m : ℕ) : 0 < and n m ↔ 0 < n ∧ 0 < m := by simp[and_eq]; by_cases 0 < n ∧ 0 < m <;> simp[*]

  induction' n with n ih <;> simp[ball, Nat.lt_succ_iff] at*
  · simp[ih]; exact ⟨
    by rintro ⟨hn, hp⟩ m hm; rcases lt_or_eq_of_le hm with (hm | rfl); { exact hp _ hm }; { exact hn },
    by intro h; exact ⟨h n (Nat.le_refl n), fun m hm => h m (le_of_lt hm)⟩⟩

informal_statement: Given an arithmetic function \( f \) and a vector function \( g \), the composition \( f \circ g \) is equivalent to applying \( f \) to each element of the vector \( g \).
informal_proof:
To prove this statement, we consider the definitions and properties of arithmetic functions and vector functions. Specifically:

1. **Arithmetic Function \( f \)**: An arithmetic function takes an integer argument and returns an integer result. In this context, it is of type \( \text{Arith}_1 m \), where \( m \) represents the domain and codomain of the function.

2. **Vector Function \( g \)**: A vector function \( g \) takes an index argument and returns an element of type \( m \). Formally, it is of type \( \text{Vec}\ n\ m \), indicating a vector with \( n \) elements from the set \( m \).

3. **Composition \( f \circ g \)**: Function composition \( f \circ g \) implies that the output of \( g \) is used as the input to \( f \). Therefore, for each index \( v \) in the domain of \( g \), \( f(g(v)) \) is well-defined.

The composition \( f \circ g \) is trivially equal to applying \( f \) to each element of \( g \). This equality holds because, for each element \( v \) in the range of \( g \), \( f(g(v)) \) directly applies \( f \) to the result of \( g(v) \).

To formalize this, consider the following steps:
- Direction: Start with an arbitrary index \( v \) in the domain of \( g \).
- Application: Apply \( g \) to \( v \) to obtain an element of type \( m \).
- Application: Apply \( f \) to the result \( g(v) \) to obtain the final result.

Since the application of \( f \) to \( g(v) \) is exactly the definition of \( f \circ g \) evaluated at \( v \), it follows that \( f \circ g \) is equivalent to applying \( f \) to each element of \( g \).

Thus, by definition of function composition and the properties of arithmetic and vector functions, the statement holds true, and the equality is confirmed.

@[simp] lemma isEqNat_pos_iff : 0 < isEqNat n m ↔ n = m := by simp[isEqNat]; by_cases n = m <;> simp[*]

/--
`List.Vector α n` is the type of lists of length `n` with elements of type `α`.

Note that there is also `Vector α n` in the root namespace,
which is the type of *arrays* of length `n` with elements of type `α`.

Typically, if you are doing programming or verification, you will primarily use `Vector α n`,
and if you are doing mathematics, you may want to use `List.Vector α n` instead.
-/

  { l : List α // l.length = n }

To prove the statement, let's break it down into manageable steps:

1. **Understand the Components**:
   - **Finite Domain `n`:** Represented by type `n` with a function `f` that operates on it.
   - **Finite Codomain `m`:** Represented by type `m` with a vector `g` that is an element of `m` with length `n`.
   
2. **Extension of Domain and Codomain**:
   - **Extended Domain `n + 1`:** Introducing a new element beyond those in `n`.
   - **Extended Codomain `m + 1`:** Introducing a new element beyond those in `m`.
   
3. **Construction of the New Function**:
   - The function `fun i => f i ::ᵥ g i` constructs a new vector or function by prepending an element to both the domain and codomain. Here, `f i` represents the value at index `i` in the new domain, and `g i` represents the corresponding value in the new codomain.

4. **Ensuring Correctness**:
   - **Application of `Fin.cases`:** This tactic is used to handle finite cases, which are essential here to handle all possible elements of the extended domain and codomain.
   - **Simplification with ` simp `:** The `simp` tactic simplifies the expressions to confirm that the new function behaves as expected across all elements of the extended domain and codomain.

5. **Conclusion of the Proof**:
   - By methodically applying these tactics, we ensure that the extended function maintains the properties of the original function and vector, thus proving that the new function is correctly defined within the extended context.

namespace Nat

lemma pos_of_eq_one (h : n = 1) : 0 < n := by simp[h]

def isEqNat (n m : ℕ) : ℕ := if n = m then 1 else 0

def isLtNat (n m : ℕ) : ℕ := if n < m then 1 else 0

def isLeNat (n m : ℕ) : ℕ := if n ≤ m then 1 else 0

def isDvdNat (n m : ℕ) : ℕ := if n ∣ m then 1 else 0

@[simp] lemma isEqNat_pos_iff : 0 < isEqNat n m ↔ n = m := by simp[isEqNat]; by_cases n = m <;> simp[*]

@[simp] lemma isLtNat_pos_iff : 0 < isLtNat n m ↔ n < m := by simp[isLtNat]; by_cases n < m <;> simp[*]

@[simp] lemma isLeNat_pos_iff : 0 < isLeNat n m ↔ n ≤ m := by simp[isLeNat]; by_cases n ≤ m <;> simp[*]

@[simp] lemma isDvdNat_pos_iff : 0 < isDvdNat n m ↔ n ∣ m := by simp[isDvdNat]; by_cases n ∣ m <;> simp[*]

def inv (n : ℕ) : ℕ := isEqNat n 0

def pos (n : ℕ) : ℕ := isLtNat 0 n

@[simp] lemma inv_zero : inv 0 = 1 := rfl

@[simp] lemma inv_iff_ne_zero : inv n = 0 ↔ 0 < n := by simp[inv, isEqNat, zero_lt_iff]

@[simp] lemma inv_ne_zero (h : n ≠ 0) : inv n = 0 := by simp[inv, isEqNat, h]

@[simp] lemma pos_zero : pos 0 = 0 := rfl

@[simp] lemma pos_ne_zero (h : n ≠ 0) : pos n = 1 := by simp[pos, isLtNat, h]

def and (n m : ℕ) : ℕ := isLtNat 0 (n * m)

def or (n m : ℕ) : ℕ := isLtNat 0 (n + m)

lemma and_eq (n m : ℕ) : and n m = if 0 < n ∧ 0 < m then 1 else 0 := by simp [mul_pos_iff, and, isLtNat]

lemma and_eq_one (n m : ℕ) : and n m = 1 ↔ 0 < n ∧ 0 < m := by simp[and_eq, imp_false, Nat.pos_iff_ne_zero]

lemma or_eq (n m : ℕ) : or n m = if 0 < n ∨ 0 < m then 1 else 0 := by simp[or, isLtNat]

@[simp] lemma and_pos_iff (n m : ℕ) : 0 < and n m ↔ 0 < n ∧ 0 < m := by simp[and_eq]; by_cases 0 < n ∧ 0 < m <;> simp[*]

@[simp] lemma or_pos_iff (n m : ℕ) : 0 < or n m ↔ 0 < n ∨ 0 < m := by simp[or_eq]; by_cases 0 < n ∨ 0 < m <;> simp[*]

@[simp] lemma inv_pos_iff (n : ℕ) : 0 < inv n ↔ ¬0 < n := by simp[inv]

@[simp] lemma pos_pos_iff (n : ℕ) : 0 < pos n ↔ 0 < n := by simp[pos]

def ball (n : ℕ) (φ : ℕ → ℕ) : ℕ := n.rec 1 (fun n ih => (φ n).pos.and ih)

@[simp] lemma ball_pos_iff {φ : ℕ → ℕ} {n : ℕ} : 0 < ball n φ ↔ ∀ m < n, 0 < φ m := by
  induction' n with n ih <;> simp[ball, Nat.lt_succ_iff] at*
  · simp[ih]; exact ⟨
    by rintro ⟨hn, hp⟩ m hm; rcases lt_or_eq_of_le hm with (hm | rfl); { exact hp _ hm }; { exact hn },
    by intro h; exact ⟨h n (Nat.le_refl n), fun m hm => h m (le_of_lt hm)⟩⟩

@[simp] lemma ball_eq_zero_iff {φ : ℕ → ℕ} {n : ℕ} : ball n φ = 0 ↔ ∃ m < n, φ m = 0 := by
  simpa[-ball_pos_iff] using not_iff_not.mpr (ball_pos_iff (φ := φ) (n := n))

lemma ball_pos_iff_eq_one {φ : ℕ → ℕ} {n : ℕ} : ball n φ = 1 ↔ 0 < ball n φ := by
  induction' n with n _ <;> simp[ball, Nat.lt_succ_iff] at*
  · constructor

/--
`List.Vector α n` is the type of lists of length `n` with elements of type `α`.

Note that there is also `Vector α n` in the root namespace,
which is the type of *arrays* of length `n` with elements of type `α`.

Typically, if you are doing programming or verification, you will primarily use `Vector α n`,
and if you are doing mathematics, you may want to use `List.Vector α n` instead.

informal_statement: For any natural number \( n \), the empty vector is downwards closed.
informal_proof: Since the empty vector contains no elements, there are no elements in it that could potentially violate a downwards closure property. By definition, downwards closure requires that if an element is in the vector, then all elements below it in the partial order are also included. lemma to_partrec' {n} {f : List.Vector ℕ n →. ℕ} (hf : ArithPart₁ f) : Partrec' f := by
  induction hf
  case zero => exact Partrec'.of_part (Partrec.const' 0)
  case one  => exact Partrec'.of_part (Partrec.const' 1)
  case add n i j =>
    exact (Partrec'.of_part ((Primrec.nat_add.comp
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j))).to_comp.partrec))
  case mul n i j =>
    exact (Partrec'.of_part ((Primrec.nat_mul.comp
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j))).to_comp.partrec))
  case proj n i =>
    exact Partrec'.of_part
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i)).to_comp.partrec
  case equal n i j =>
    have : Primrec (fun (v : List.Vector ℕ n) => if v.get i = v.get j then 1 else 0) :=
      Primrec.ite

lemma to_partrec' {n} {f : List.Vector ℕ n →. ℕ} (hf : ArithPart₁ f) : Partrec' f := by
  induction hf
  case zero => exact Partrec'.of_part (Partrec.const' 0)
  case one  => exact Partrec'.of_part (Partrec.const' 1)
  case add n i j =>
    exact (Partrec'.of_part ((Primrec.nat_add.comp
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j))).to_comp.partrec))
  case mul n i j =>
    exact (Partrec'.of_part ((Primrec.nat_mul.comp
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j))).to_comp.partrec))
  case proj n i =>
    exact Partrec'.of_part
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i)).to_comp.partrec
  case equal n i j =>
    have : Primrec (fun (v : List.Vector ℕ n) => if v.get i = v.get j then 1 else 0) :=
      Primrec.ite
        (Primrec.eq.comp
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j)))
        (_root_.Primrec.const 1)
        (_root_.Primrec.const 0)
    exact Partrec'.of_part this.to_comp.partrec
  case lt n i j =>
    have : Primrec (fun (v : List.Vector ℕ n) => if v.get i < v.get j then 1 else 0) :=
      Primrec.ite
        (Primrec.nat_lt.comp
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j)))
        (_root_.Primrec.const 1)
        (_root_.Primrec.const 0)
    exact Partrec'.of_part this.to_comp.partrec
  case comp m n f g _ _ hf hg =>
    exact Partrec'.comp g hf hg
  case rfind f _ hf =>
    exact Partrec'.rfind hf

@[simp] lemma ball_pos_iff {φ : ℕ → ℕ} {n : ℕ} : 0 < ball n φ ↔ ∀ m < n, 0 < φ m := by
  induction' n with n ih <;> simp[ball, Nat.lt_succ_iff] at*
  · simp[ih]; exact ⟨
    by rintro ⟨hn, hp⟩ m hm; rcases lt_or_eq_of_le hm with (hm | rfl); { exact hp _ hm }; { exact hn },
    by intro h; exact ⟨h n (Nat.le_refl n), fun m hm => h m (le_of_lt hm)⟩⟩

C0_dependencies.name: Nat.ball_eq_zero_iff
C0_dependencies.content:
@[simp] lemma ball_eq_zero_iff {φ : ℕ → ℕ} {n : ℕ} : ball n φ = 0 ↔ ∃ m < n, φ m = 0 := by
  simpa[-ball_pos_iff] using not_iff_not.mpr (ball_pos_iff (φ := φ) (n := n))

lemma to_partrec' {n} {f : List.Vector ℕ n →. ℕ} (hf : ArithPart₁ f) : Partrec' f := by
  induction hf
  case zero => exact Partrec'.of_part (Partrec.const' 0)
  case one  => exact Partrec'.of_part (Partrec.const' 1)
  case add n i j =>
    exact (Partrec'.of_part ((Primrec.nat_add.comp
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j))).to_comp.partrec))
  case mul n i j =>
    exact (Partrec'.of_part ((Primrec.nat_mul.comp
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j))).to_comp.partrec))
  case proj n i =>
    exact Partrec'.of_part
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i)).to_comp.partrec
  case equal n i j =>
    have : Primrec (fun (v : List.Vector ℕ n) => if v.get i = v.get j then 1 else 0) :=
      Primrec.ite
        (Primrec.eq.comp
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j)))
        (_root_.Primrec.const 1)
        (_root_.Primrec.const 0)
    exact Partrec'.of_part this.to_comp.partrec
  case lt n i j =>
    have : Primrec (fun (v : List.Vector ℕ n) => if v.get i < v.get j then 1 else 0) :=
      Primrec.ite
        (Primrec.nat_lt.comp
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j)))
        (_root_.Primrec.const 1)
        (_root_.Primrec.const 0)
    exact Partrec'.of_part this.to_comp.partrec
  case comp m n f g _ _ hf hg =>
    exact Partrec'.comp g hf hg
  case rfind f _ hf =>
    exact Partrec'.rfind hf

lemma bind (f : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ →. ℕ) (hf : @ArithPart₁ (n + 1) fun v => f v.tail v.head) {g} (hg : @ArithPart₁ n g) :
    @ArithPart₁ n fun v => (g v).bind (f v) :=
  (hf.comp (g :> fun i v => v.get i) (fun i => by cases i using Fin.cases <;> simp[*]; exact proj _)).of_eq (by
    intro v; simp
    rcases Part.eq_none_or_eq_some (g v) with (hgv | ⟨x, hgv⟩)
    · simp[hgv, List.Vector.mOfFn]
    · simp[hgv, Matrix.comp_vecCons']
      have : List.Vector.mOfFn (fun i => (g :> fun j v => Part.some $ v.get j) i v) = pure (List.Vector.ofFn (x :> fun j => v.get j)) := by
        rw[←List.Vector.mOfFn_pure]; apply congr_arg
        funext i; cases i using Fin.cases <;> simp[hgv]
      simp[this])

open Primrec

lemma to_partrec' {n} {f : List.Vector ℕ n →. ℕ} (hf : ArithPart₁ f) : Partrec' f := by
  induction hf
  case zero => exact Partrec'.of_part (Partrec.const' 0)
  case one  => exact Partrec'.of_part (Partrec.const' 1)
  case add n i j =>
    exact (Partrec'.of_part ((Primrec.nat_add.comp
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j))).to_comp.partrec))
  case mul n i j =>
    exact (Partrec'.of_part ((Primrec.nat_mul.comp
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j))).to_comp.partrec))
  case proj n i =>
    exact Partrec'.of_part
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i)).to_comp.partrec
  case equal n i j =>
    have : Primrec (fun (v : List.Vector ℕ n) => if v.get i = v.get j then 1 else 0) :=
      Primrec.ite
        (Primrec.eq.comp
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j)))
        (_root_.Primrec.const 1)
        (_root_.Primrec.const 0)
    exact Partrec'.of_part this.to_comp.partrec
  case lt n i j =>
    have : Primrec (fun (v : List.Vector ℕ n) => if v.get i < v.get j then 1 else 0) :=
      Primrec.ite
        (Primrec.nat_lt.comp
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j)))
        (_root_.Primrec.const 1)
        (_root_.Primrec.const 0)
    exact Partrec'.of_part this.to_comp.partrec
  case comp m n f g _ _ hf hg =>
    exact Partrec'.comp g hf hg
  case rfind f _ hf =>
    exact Partrec'.rfind hf

lemma of_eq {n} {f g : List.Vector ℕ n →. ℕ} (hf : ArithPart₁ f) (H : ∀ i, f i = g i) : ArithPart₁ g :=
  (funext H : f = g) ▸ hf

lemma bind (f : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ →. ℕ) (hf : @ArithPart₁ (n + 1) fun v => f v.tail v.head) {g} (hg : @ArithPart₁ n g) :
    @ArithPart₁ n fun v => (g v).bind (f v) :=
  (hf.comp (g :> fun i v => v.get i) (fun i => by cases i using Fin.cases <;> simp[*]; exact proj _)).of_eq (by
    intro v; simp
    rcases Part.eq_none_or_eq_some (g v) with (hgv | ⟨x, hgv⟩)
    · simp[hgv, List.Vector.mOfFn]
    · simp[hgv, Matrix.comp_vecCons']
      have : List.Vector.mOfFn (fun i => (g :> fun j v => Part.some $ v.get j) i v) = pure (List.Vector.ofFn (x :> fun j => v.get j)) := by
        rw[←List.Vector.mOfFn_pure]; apply congr_arg
        funext i; cases i using Fin.cases <;> simp[hgv]
      simp[this])

lemma map (f : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ → ℕ) (hf : @Arith₁ (n + 1) fun v => f v.tail v.head) {g} (hg : @ArithPart₁ n g) :
    @ArithPart₁ n fun v => (g v).map (f v) :=
  (bind (Part.some $ f · ·) (hf.of_eq <| by simp) hg).of_eq <| by
  intro v; rcases Part.eq_none_or_eq_some (g v) with (_ | ⟨x, _⟩) <;> simp[*]

lemma comp₁ (f : ℕ →. ℕ) (hf : @ArithPart₁ 1 fun v => f (v.get 0)) {n g} (hg : @Arith₁ n g) :
    @ArithPart₁ n fun v => f (g v) :=
  (hf.comp _ fun _ => hg).of_eq (by simp)

lemma comp₂ (f : ℕ → ℕ →. ℕ) (hf : @ArithPart₁ 2 fun v => f (v.get 0) (v.get 1)) {n g h} (hg : @Arith₁ n g) (hh : @Arith₁ n h) :
    @ArithPart₁ n fun v => f (g v) (h v) :=
  (hf.comp ![g, h] (fun i => i.cases hg (fun i => by simpa using hh))).of_eq
    (by intro i
        have : (fun j => (![↑g, h] : Fin 2 → List.Vector ℕ n →. ℕ) j i) = (fun j => pure (![g i, h i] j)) := by
          funext j; cases j using Fin.cases <;> simp[Fin.eq_zero]
        simp[Matrix.comp_vecCons']; simp[this] )

lemma rfind' {n} {f : ℕ → List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ} (h : Arith₁ (n := n + 1) (fun v => f v.head v.tail)) :

lemma to_partrec' {n} {f : List.Vector ℕ n →. ℕ} (hf : ArithPart₁ f) : Partrec' f := by
  induction hf
  case zero => exact Partrec'.of_part (Partrec.const' 0)
  case one  => exact Partrec'.of_part (Partrec.const' 1)
  case add n i j =>
    exact (Partrec'.of_part ((Primrec.nat_add.comp
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j))).to_comp.partrec))
  case mul n i j =>
    exact (Partrec'.of_part ((Primrec.nat_mul.comp
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j))).to_comp.partrec))
  case proj n i =>
    exact Partrec'.of_part
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i)).to_comp.partrec
  case equal n i j =>
    have : Primrec (fun (v : List.Vector ℕ n) => if v.get i = v.get j then 1 else 0) :=
      Primrec.ite
        (Primrec.eq.comp
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j)))
        (_root_.Primrec.const 1)
        (_root_.Primrec.const 0)
    exact Partrec'.of_part this.to_comp.partrec
  case lt n i j =>
    have : Primrec (fun (v : List.Vector ℕ n) => if v.get i < v.get j then 1 else 0) :=
      Primrec.ite
        (Primrec.nat_lt.comp
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j)))
        (_root_.Primrec.const 1)
        (_root_.Primrec.const 0)
    exact Partrec'.of_part this.to_comp.partrec
  case comp m n f g _ _ hf hg =>
    exact Partrec'.comp g hf hg
  case rfind f _ hf =>
    exact Partrec'.rfind hf

        rw[←List.Vector.mOfFn_pure]; apply congr_arg
        funext i; cases i using Fin.cases <;> simp[hgv]
      simp[this])

lemma pos_of_eq_one (h : n = 1) : 0 < n := by simp[h]

def isEqNat (n m : ℕ) : ℕ := if n = m then 1 else 0

def isLtNat (n m : ℕ) : ℕ := if n < m then 1 else 0

def isLeNat (n m : ℕ) : ℕ := if n ≤ m then 1 else 0

def isDvdNat (n m : ℕ) : ℕ := if n ∣ m then 1 else 0

@[simp] lemma isEqNat_pos_iff : 0 < isEqNat n m ↔ n = m := by simp[isEqNat]; by_cases n = m <;> simp[*]

@[simp] lemma isLtNat_pos_iff : 0 < isLtNat n m ↔ n < m := by simp[isLtNat]; by_cases n < m <;> simp[*]

@[simp] lemma isLeNat_pos_iff : 0 < isLeNat n m ↔ n ≤ m := by simp[isLeNat]; by_cases n ≤ m <;> simp[*]

@[simp] lemma isDvdNat_pos_iff : 0 < isDvdNat n m ↔ n ∣ m := by simp[isDvdNat]; by_cases n ∣ m <;> simp[*]

def inv (n : ℕ) : ℕ := isEqNat n 0

def pos (n : ℕ) : ℕ := isLtNat 0 n

@[simp] lemma inv_zero : inv 0 = 1 := rfl

@[simp] lemma inv_iff_ne_zero : inv n = 0 ↔ 0 < n := by simp[inv, isEqNat, zero_lt_iff]

@[simp] lemma inv_ne_zero (h : n ≠ 0) : inv n = 0 := by simp[inv, isEqNat, h]

@[simp] lemma pos_zero : pos 0 = 0 := rfl

@[simp] lemma pos_ne_zero (h : n ≠ 0) : pos n = 1 := by simp[pos, isLtNat, h]

def and (n m : ℕ) : ℕ := isLtNat 0 (n * m)

def or (n m : ℕ) : ℕ := isLtNat 0 (n + m)

lemma and_eq (n m : ℕ) : and n m = if 0 < n ∧ 0 < m then 1 else 0 := by simp [mul_pos_iff, and, isLtNat]

lemma and_eq_one (n m : ℕ) : and n m = 1 ↔ 0 < n ∧ 0 < m := by simp[and_eq, imp_false, Nat.pos_iff_ne_zero]

lemma or_eq (n m : ℕ) : or n m = if 0 < n ∨ 0 < m then 1 else 0 := by simp[or, isLtNat]

@[simp] lemma and_pos_iff (n m : ℕ) : 0 < and n m ↔ 0 < n ∧ 0 < m := by simp[and_eq]; by_cases 0 < n ∧ 0 < m <;> simp[*]

@[simp] lemma or_pos_iff (n m : ℕ) : 0 < or n m ↔ 0 < n ∨ 0 < m := by simp[or_eq]; by_cases 0 < n ∨ 0 < m <;> simp[*]

@[simp] lemma inv_pos_iff (n : ℕ) : 0 < inv n ↔ ¬0 < n := by simp[inv]

@[simp] lemma pos_pos_iff (n : ℕ) : 0 < pos n ↔ 0 < n := by simp[pos]

def ball (n : ℕ) (φ : ℕ → ℕ) : ℕ := n.rec 1 (fun n ih => (φ n).pos.and ih)

@[simp] lemma ball_pos_iff {φ : ℕ → ℕ} {n : ℕ} : 0 < ball n φ ↔ ∀ m < n, 0 < φ m := by
  induction' n with n ih <;> simp[ball, Nat.lt_succ_iff] at*
  · simp[ih]; exact ⟨
    by rintro ⟨hn, hp⟩ m hm; rcases lt_or_eq_of_le hm with (hm | rfl); { exact hp _ hm }; { exact hn },
    by intro h; exact ⟨h n (Nat.le_refl n), fun m hm => h m (le_of_lt hm)⟩⟩

@[simp] lemma ball_eq_zero_iff {φ : ℕ → ℕ} {n : ℕ} : ball n φ = 0 ↔ ∃ m < n, φ m = 0 := by
  simpa[-ball_pos_iff] using not_iff_not.mpr (ball_pos_iff (φ := φ) (n := n))

lemma ball_pos_iff_eq_one {φ : ℕ → ℕ} {n : ℕ} : ball n φ = 1 ↔ 0 < ball n φ := by
  induction' n with n _ <;> simp[ball, Nat.lt_succ_iff] at*
  · constructor
    · intro h; simpa using pos_of_eq_one h
    · intro h; simpa[and_eq_one] using h

inductive ArithPart₁ : ∀ {n}, (List.Vector ℕ n →. ℕ) → Prop
  | zero {n} : @ArithPart₁ n (fun _ => 0)
  | one {n} : @ArithPart₁ n (fun _ => 1)
  | add {n} (i j : Fin n) : @ArithPart₁ n (fun v => v.get i + v.get j : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ)
  | mul {n} (i j : Fin n) : @ArithPart₁ n (fun v => v.get i * v.get j : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ)
  | proj {n} (i : Fin n) : @ArithPart₁ n (fun v => v.get i : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ)
  | equal {n} (i j : Fin n) : @ArithPart₁ n (fun v => isEqNat (v.get i) (v.get j) : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ)
  | lt {n} (i j : Fin n) : @ArithPart₁ n (fun v => isLtNat (v.get i) (v.get j) : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ)
  | comp {m n f} (g : Fin n → List.Vector ℕ m →. ℕ) :
    ArithPart₁ f → (∀ i, ArithPart₁ (g i)) → ArithPart₁ fun v => (List.Vector.mOfFn fun i => g i v) >>= f
  | rfind {n} {f : List.Vector ℕ (n + 1) → ℕ} :
    ArithPart₁ (n := n + 1) f → ArithPart₁ (fun v => rfind fun n => Part.some (f (n ::ᵥ v) = 0))

def Arith₁ (f : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ) := ArithPart₁ (n := n) f

end Nat

open Primrec

lemma to_partrec' {n} {f : List.Vector ℕ n →. ℕ} (hf : ArithPart₁ f) : Partrec' f := by
  induction hf
  case zero => exact Partrec'.of_part (Partrec.const' 0)
  case one  => exact Partrec'.of_part (Partrec.const' 1)
  case add n i j =>
    exact (Partrec'.of_part ((Primrec.nat_add.comp
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j))).to_comp.partrec))
  case mul n i j =>
    exact (Partrec'.of_part ((Primrec.nat_mul.comp
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j))).to_comp.partrec))
  case proj n i =>
    exact Partrec'.of_part
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i)).to_comp.partrec
  case equal n i j =>
    have : Primrec (fun (v : List.Vector ℕ n) => if v.get i = v.get j then 1 else 0) :=
      Primrec.ite
        (Primrec.eq.comp
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j)))
        (_root_.Primrec.const 1)
        (_root_.Primrec.const 0)
    exact Partrec'.of_part this.to_comp.partrec
  case lt n i j =>
    have : Primrec (fun (v : List.Vector ℕ n) => if v.get i < v.get j then 1 else 0) :=
      Primrec.ite
        (Primrec.nat_lt.comp
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j)))
        (_root_.Primrec.const 1)
        (_root_.Primrec.const 0)
    exact Partrec'.of_part this.to_comp.partrec
  case comp m n f g _ _ hf hg =>
    exact Partrec'.comp g hf hg
  case rfind f _ hf =>
    exact Partrec'.rfind hf

lemma of_eq {n} {f g : List.Vector ℕ n →. ℕ} (hf : ArithPart₁ f) (H : ∀ i, f i = g i) : ArithPart₁ g :=
  (funext H : f = g) ▸ hf

lemma bind (f : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ →. ℕ) (hf : @ArithPart₁ (n + 1) fun v => f v.tail v.head) {g} (hg : @ArithPart₁ n g) :
    @ArithPart₁ n fun v => (g v).bind (f v) :=
  (hf.comp (g :> fun i v => v.get i) (fun i => by cases i using Fin.cases <;> simp[*]; exact proj _)).of_eq (by
    intro v; simp
    rcases Part.eq_none_or_eq_some (g v) with (hgv | ⟨x, hgv⟩)
    · simp[hgv, List.Vector.mOfFn]
    · simp[hgv, Matrix.comp_vecCons']
      have : List.Vector.mOfFn (fun i => (g :> fun j v => Part.some $ v.get j) i v) = pure (List.Vector.ofFn (x :> fun j => v.get j)) := by
        rw[←List.Vector.mOfFn_pure]; apply congr_arg
        funext i; cases i using Fin.cases <;> simp[hgv]
      simp[this])

    @ArithPart₁ n fun v => (g v).map (f v) :=
  (bind (Part.some $ f · ·) (hf.of_eq <| by simp) hg).of_eq <| by

    @ArithPart₁ n fun v => f (g v) :=

          funext j; cases j using Fin.cases <;> simp[Fin.eq_zero]

    ArithPart₁ (fun v => Nat.rfind fun n => Part.some (f n v = 0)) := rfind h

lemma rfind'₁ {n} (i : Fin n) {f : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ} (h : Arith₁ (n := 2) (fun v => f (v.get 0) (v.get 1))) :

lemma to_partrec' {n} {f : List.Vector ℕ n →. ℕ} (hf : ArithPart₁ f) : Partrec' f := by
  induction hf
  case zero => exact Partrec'.of_part (Partrec.const' 0)
  case one  => exact Partrec'.of_part (Partrec.const' 1)
  case add n i j =>
    exact (Partrec'.of_part ((Primrec.nat_add.comp
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j))).to_comp.partrec))
  case mul n i j =>
    exact (Partrec'.of_part ((Primrec.nat_mul.comp
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j))).to_comp.partrec))
  case proj n i =>
    exact Partrec'.of_part
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i)).to_comp.partrec
  case equal n i j =>
    have : Primrec (fun (v : List.Vector ℕ n) => if v.get i = v.get j then 1 else 0) :=
      Primrec.ite
        (Primrec.eq.comp
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j)))
        (_root_.Primrec.const 1)
        (_root_.Primrec.const 0)
    exact Partrec'.of_part this.to_comp.partrec
  case lt n i j =>
    have : Primrec (fun (v : List.Vector ℕ n) => if v.get i < v.get j then 1 else 0) :=
      Primrec.ite
        (Primrec.nat_lt.comp
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j)))
        (_root_.Primrec.const 1)
        (_root_.Primrec.const 0)
    exact Partrec'.of_part this.to_comp.partrec
  case comp m n f g _ _ hf hg =>
    exact Partrec'.comp g hf hg
  case rfind f _ hf =>
    exact Partrec'.rfind hf

lemma bind (f : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ →. ℕ) (hf : @ArithPart₁ (n + 1) fun v => f v.tail v.head) {g} (hg : @ArithPart₁ n g) :
    @ArithPart₁ n fun v => (g v).bind (f v) :=
  (hf.comp (g :> fun i v => v.get i) (fun i => by cases i using Fin.cases <;> simp[*]; exact proj _)).of_eq (by
    intro v; simp
    rcases Part.eq_none_or_eq_some (g v) with (hgv | ⟨x, hgv⟩)
    · simp[hgv, List.Vector.mOfFn]
    · simp[hgv, Matrix.comp_vecCons']
      have : List.Vector.mOfFn (fun i => (g :> fun j v => Part.some $ v.get j) i v) = pure (List.Vector.ofFn (x :> fun j => v.get j)) := by
        rw[←List.Vector.mOfFn_pure]; apply congr_arg
        funext i; cases i using Fin.cases <;> simp[hgv]
      simp[this])

  | proj {n} (i : Fin n) : @ArithPart₁ n (fun v => v.get i : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ)
  | equal {n} (i j : Fin n) : @ArithPart₁ n (fun v => isEqNat (v.get i) (v.get j) : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ)

        (_root_.Primrec.const 1)

open Primrec

lemma to_partrec' {n} {f : List.Vector ℕ n →. ℕ} (hf : ArithPart₁ f) : Partrec' f := by
  induction hf
  case zero => exact Partrec'.of_part (Partrec.const' 0)
  case one  => exact Partrec'.of_part (Partrec.const' 1)
  case add n i j =>
    exact (Partrec'.of_part ((Primrec.nat_add.comp
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j))).to_comp.partrec))
  case mul n i j =>
    exact (Partrec'.of_part ((Primrec.nat_mul.comp
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j))).to_comp.partrec))
  case proj n i =>
    exact Partrec'.of_part
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i)).to_comp.partrec
  case equal n i j =>
    have : Primrec (fun (v : List.Vector ℕ n) => if v.get i = v.get j then 1 else 0) :=
      Primrec.ite
        (Primrec.eq.comp
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j)))
        (_root_.Primrec.const 1)
        (_root_.Primrec.const 0)
    exact Partrec'.of_part this.to_comp.partrec
  case lt n i j =>
    have : Primrec (fun (v : List.Vector ℕ n) => if v.get i < v.get j then 1 else 0) :=
      Primrec.ite
        (Primrec.nat_lt.comp
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j)))
        (_root_.Primrec.const 1)
        (_root_.Primrec.const 0)
    exact Partrec'.of_part this.to_comp.partrec
  case comp m n f g _ _ hf hg =>
    exact Partrec'.comp g hf hg
  case rfind f _ hf =>
    exact Partrec'.rfind hf

lemma of_eq {n} {f g : List.Vector ℕ n →. ℕ} (hf : ArithPart₁ f) (H : ∀ i, f i = g i) : ArithPart₁ g :=
  (funext H : f = g) ▸ hf

lemma bind (f : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ →. ℕ) (hf : @ArithPart₁ (n + 1) fun v => f v.tail v.head) {g} (hg : @ArithPart₁ n g) :
    @ArithPart₁ n fun v => (g v).bind (f v) :=
  (hf.comp (g :> fun i v => v.get i) (fun i => by cases i using Fin.cases <;> simp[*]; exact proj _)).of_eq (by
    intro v; simp
    rcases Part.eq_none_or_eq_some (g v) with (hgv | ⟨x, hgv⟩)
    · simp[hgv, List.Vector.mOfFn]
    · simp[hgv, Matrix.comp_vecCons']
      have : List.Vector.mOfFn (fun i => (g :> fun j v => Part.some $ v.get j) i v) = pure (List.Vector.ofFn (x :> fun j => v.get j)) := by
        rw[←List.Vector.mOfFn_pure]; apply congr_arg
        funext i; cases i using Fin.cases <;> simp[hgv]
      simp[this])

lemma map (f : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ → ℕ) (hf : @Arith₁ (n + 1) fun v => f v.tail v.head) {g} (hg : @ArithPart₁ n g) :
    @ArithPart₁ n fun v => (g v).map (f v) :=
  (bind (Part.some $ f · ·) (hf.of_eq <| by simp) hg).of_eq <| by
  intro v; rcases Part.eq_none_or_eq_some (g v) with (_ | ⟨x, _⟩) <;> simp[*]

lemma comp₁ (f : ℕ →. ℕ) (hf : @ArithPart₁ 1 fun v => f (v.get 0)) {n g} (hg : @Arith₁ n g) :
    @ArithPart₁ n fun v => f (g v) :=
  (hf.comp _ fun _ => hg).of_eq (by simp)

lemma comp₂ (f : ℕ → ℕ →. ℕ) (hf : @ArithPart₁ 2 fun v => f (v.get 0) (v.get 1)) {n g h} (hg : @Arith₁ n g) (hh : @Arith₁ n h) :
    @ArithPart₁ n fun v => f (g v) (h v) :=
  (hf.comp ![g, h] (fun i => i.cases hg (fun i => by simpa using hh))).of_eq
    (by intro i
        have : (fun j => (![↑g, h] : Fin 2 → List.Vector ℕ n →. ℕ) j i) = (fun j => pure (![g i, h i] j)) := by
          funext j; cases j using Fin.cases <;> simp[Fin.eq_zero]
        simp[Matrix.comp_vecCons']; simp[this] )

lemma rfind' {n} {f : ℕ → List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ} (h : Arith₁ (n := n + 1) (fun v => f v.head v.tail)) :
    ArithPart₁ (fun v => Nat.rfind fun n => Part.some (f n v = 0)) := rfind h

lemma rfind'₁ {n} (i : Fin n) {f : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ} (h : Arith₁ (n := 2) (fun v => f (v.get 0) (v.get 1))) :
    ArithPart₁ (fun v => Nat.rfind fun n => Part.some (f n (v.get i) = 0)) :=
  (rfind h).comp₁ (fun m => Nat.rfind fun n => Part.some (f n m = 0)) (proj i)

/--
`List.Vector α n` is the type of lists of length `n` with elements of type `α`.

Note that there is also `Vector α n` in the root namespace,
which is the type of *arrays* of length `n` with elements of type `α`.

Typically, if you are doing programming or verification, you will primarily use `Vector α n`,
and if you are doing mathematics, you may want to use `List.Vector α n` instead.
-/

  { l : List α // l.length = n }

  induction hf
  case zero => exact Partrec'.of_part (Partrec.const' 0)
  case one  => exact Partrec'.of_part (Partrec.const' 1)
  case add n i j =>
    exact (Partrec'.of_part ((Primrec.nat_add.comp
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j))).to_comp.partrec))
  case mul n i j =>
    exact (Partrec'.of_part ((Primrec.nat_mul.comp
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j))).to_comp.partrec))
  case proj n i =>
    exact Partrec'.of_part
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i)).to_comp.partrec
  case equal n i j =>
    have : Primrec (fun (v : List.Vector ℕ n) => if v.get i = v.get j then 1 else 0) :=
      Primrec.ite
        (Primrec.eq.comp
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j)))
        (_root_.Primrec.const 1)
        (_root_.Primrec.const 0)
    exact Partrec'.of_part this.to_comp.partrec
  case lt n i j =>
    have : Primrec (fun (v : List.Vector ℕ n) => if v.get i < v.get j then 1 else 0) :=
      Primrec.ite
        (Primrec.nat_lt.comp
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j)))
        (_root_.Primrec.const 1)
        (_root_.Primrec.const 0)
    exact Partrec'.of_part this.to_comp.partrec
  case comp m n f g _ _ hf hg =>
    exact Partrec'.comp g hf hg
  case rfind f _ hf =>
    exact Partrec'.rfind hf

informal_statement: For all indices $i$ and $j$ in the range from $0$ to $n-1$, the product of the $i$-th and $j$-th elements of the vector $v$ belongs to the set $\text{ArithPart}_1$.
informal_proof: Given that both $v.get\ i$ and $v.get\ j$ are elements of $\text{ArithPart}_1$, and assuming that multiplication is closed within this set, their product $v.get\ i \times v.get\ j$ will also be an element of $\text{ArithPart}_1$. Therefore, by the closure property of multiplication in $\text{ArithPart}_1$, the lemma holds true.

def isDvdNat (n m : ℕ) : ℕ := if n ∣ m then 1 else 0

@[simp] lemma isLtNat_pos_iff : 0 < isLtNat n m ↔ n < m := by simp[isLtNat]; by_cases n < m <;> simp[*]

@[simp] lemma isLeNat_pos_iff : 0 < isLeNat n m ↔ n ≤ m := by simp[isLeNat]; by_cases n ≤ m <;> simp[*]

@[simp] lemma isDvdNat_pos_iff : 0 < isDvdNat n m ↔ n ∣ m := by simp[isDvdNat]; by_cases n ∣ m <;> simp[*]

def pos (n : ℕ) : ℕ := isLtNat 0 n

@[simp] lemma inv_zero : inv 0 = 1 := rfl

@[simp] lemma inv_ne_zero (h : n ≠ 0) : inv n = 0 := by simp[inv, isEqNat, h]

@[simp] lemma pos_ne_zero (h : n ≠ 0) : pos n = 1 := by simp[pos, isLtNat, h]

def or (n m : ℕ) : ℕ := isLtNat 0 (n + m)

lemma and_eq (n m : ℕ) : and n m = if 0 < n ∧ 0 < m then 1 else 0 := by simp [mul_pos_iff, and, isLtNat]

lemma and_eq_one (n m : ℕ) : and n m = 1 ↔ 0 < n ∧ 0 < m := by simp[and_eq, imp_false, Nat.pos_iff_ne_zero]

lemma or_eq (n m : ℕ) : or n m = if 0 < n ∨ 0 < m then 1 else 0 := by simp[or, isLtNat]

@[simp] lemma and_pos_iff (n m : ℕ) : 0 < and n m ↔ 0 < n ∧ 0 < m := by simp[and_eq]; by_cases 0 < n ∧ 0 < m <;> simp[*]

@[simp] lemma or_pos_iff (n m : ℕ) : 0 < or n m ↔ 0 < n ∨ 0 < m := by simp[or_eq]; by_cases 0 < n ∨ 0 < m <;> simp[*]

  · simp[ih]; exact ⟨
    by rintro ⟨hn, hp⟩ m hm; rcases lt_or_eq_of_le hm with (hm | rfl); { exact hp _ hm }; { exact hn },

    · intro h; simpa using pos_of_eq_one h
    · intro h; simpa[and_eq_one] using h

inductive ArithPart₁ : ∀ {n}, (List.Vector ℕ n →. ℕ) → Prop
  | zero {n} : @ArithPart₁ n (fun _ => 0)
  | one {n} : @ArithPart₁ n (fun _ => 1)
  | add {n} (i j : Fin n) : @ArithPart₁ n (fun v => v.get i + v.get j : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ)
  | mul {n} (i j : Fin n) : @ArithPart₁ n (fun v => v.get i * v.get j : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ)
  | proj {n} (i : Fin n) : @ArithPart₁ n (fun v => v.get i : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ)
  | equal {n} (i j : Fin n) : @ArithPart₁ n (fun v => isEqNat (v.get i) (v.get j) : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ)
  | lt {n} (i j : Fin n) : @ArithPart₁ n (fun v => isLtNat (v.get i) (v.get j) : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ)
  | comp {m n f} (g : Fin n → List.Vector ℕ m →. ℕ) :
    ArithPart₁ f → (∀ i, ArithPart₁ (g i)) → ArithPart₁ fun v => (List.Vector.mOfFn fun i => g i v) >>= f
  | rfind {n} {f : List.Vector ℕ (n + 1) → ℕ} :
    ArithPart₁ (n := n + 1) f → ArithPart₁ (fun v => rfind fun n => Part.some (f (n ::ᵥ v) = 0))

def Arith₁ (f : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ) := ArithPart₁ (n := n) f

open Primrec

lemma to_partrec' {n} {f : List.Vector ℕ n →. ℕ} (hf : ArithPart₁ f) : Partrec' f := by
  induction hf
  case zero => exact Partrec'.of_part (Partrec.const' 0)
  case one  => exact Partrec'.of_part (Partrec.const' 1)
  case add n i j =>
    exact (Partrec'.of_part ((Primrec.nat_add.comp
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j))).to_comp.partrec))
  case mul n i j =>
    exact (Partrec'.of_part ((Primrec.nat_mul.comp
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j))).to_comp.partrec))
  case proj n i =>
    exact Partrec'.of_part
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i)).to_comp.partrec
  case equal n i j =>
    have : Primrec (fun (v : List.Vector ℕ n) => if v.get i = v.get j then 1 else 0) :=
      Primrec.ite
        (Primrec.eq.comp
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j)))
        (_root_.Primrec.const 1)
        (_root_.Primrec.const 0)
    exact Partrec'.of_part this.to_comp.partrec
  case lt n i j =>
    have : Primrec (fun (v : List.Vector ℕ n) => if v.get i < v.get j then 1 else 0) :=
      Primrec.ite
        (Primrec.nat_lt.comp
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j)))
        (_root_.Primrec.const 1)
        (_root_.Primrec.const 0)
    exact Partrec'.of_part this.to_comp.partrec
  case comp m n f g _ _ hf hg =>
    exact Partrec'.comp g hf hg
  case rfind f _ hf =>
    exact Partrec'.rfind hf

lemma of_eq {n} {f g : List.Vector ℕ n →. ℕ} (hf : ArithPart₁ f) (H : ∀ i, f i = g i) : ArithPart₁ g :=
  (funext H : f = g) ▸ hf

lemma bind (f : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ →. ℕ) (hf : @ArithPart₁ (n + 1) fun v => f v.tail v.head) {g} (hg : @ArithPart₁ n g) :
    @ArithPart₁ n fun v => (g v).bind (f v) :=
  (hf.comp (g :> fun i v => v.get i) (fun i => by cases i using Fin.cases <;> simp[*]; exact proj _)).of_eq (by
    intro v; simp
    rcases Part.eq_none_or_eq_some (g v) with (hgv | ⟨x, hgv⟩)
    · simp[hgv, List.Vector.mOfFn]
    · simp[hgv, Matrix.comp_vecCons']
      have : List.Vector.mOfFn (fun i => (g :> fun j v => Part.some $ v.get j) i v) = pure (List.Vector.ofFn (x :> fun j => v.get j)) := by
        rw[←List.Vector.mOfFn_pure]; apply congr_arg
        funext i; cases i using Fin.cases <;> simp[hgv]
      simp[this])

lemma map (f : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ → ℕ) (hf : @Arith₁ (n + 1) fun v => f v.tail v.head) {g} (hg : @ArithPart₁ n g) :
    @ArithPart₁ n fun v => (g v).map (f v) :=
  (bind (Part.some $ f · ·) (hf.of_eq <| by simp) hg).of_eq <| by
  intro v; rcases Part.eq_none_or_eq_some (g v) with (_ | ⟨x, _⟩) <;> simp[*]

lemma comp₁ (f : ℕ →. ℕ) (hf : @ArithPart₁ 1 fun v => f (v.get 0)) {n g} (hg : @Arith₁ n g) :
    @ArithPart₁ n fun v => f (g v) :=
  (hf.comp _ fun _ => hg).of_eq (by simp)

lemma comp₂ (f : ℕ → ℕ →. ℕ) (hf : @ArithPart₁ 2 fun v => f (v.get 0) (v.get 1)) {n g h} (hg : @Arith₁ n g) (hh : @Arith₁ n h) :
    @ArithPart₁ n fun v => f (g v) (h v) :=
  (hf.comp ![g, h] (fun i => i.cases hg (fun i => by simpa using hh))).of_eq
    (by intro i
        have : (fun j => (![↑g, h] : Fin 2 → List.Vector ℕ n →. ℕ) j i) = (fun j => pure (![g i, h i] j)) := by
          funext j; cases j using Fin.cases <;> simp[Fin.eq_zero]
        simp[Matrix.comp_vecCons']; simp[this] )

lemma rfind' {n} {f : ℕ → List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ} (h : Arith₁ (n := n + 1) (fun v => f v.head v.tail)) :
    ArithPart₁ (fun v => Nat.rfind fun n => Part.some (f n v = 0)) := rfind h

lemma rfind'₁ {n} (i : Fin n) {f : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ} (h : Arith₁ (n := 2) (fun v => f (v.get 0) (v.get 1))) :
    ArithPart₁ (fun v => Nat.rfind fun n => Part.some (f n (v.get i) = 0)) :=
  (rfind h).comp₁ (fun m => Nat.rfind fun n => Part.some (f n m = 0)) (proj i)

end Nat.ArithPart₁

namespace Nat.Arith₁

lemma of_eq {n} {f g : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ} (hf : Arith₁ f) (H : ∀ i, f i = g i) : Arith₁ g :=
  (funext H : f = g) ▸ hf

lemma zero {n} : @Arith₁ n (fun _ => 0 : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ) := by exact?

/--
`List.Vector α n` is the type of lists of length `n` with elements of type `α`.

Note that there is also `Vector α n` in the root namespace,
which is the type of *arrays* of length `n` with elements of type `α`.

Typically, if you are doing programming or verification, you will primarily use `Vector α n`,
and if you are doing mathematics, you may want to use `List.Vector α n` instead.
-/
def List.Vector (α : Type u) (n : ℕ) :=
  { l : List α // l.length = n }

lemma pos_of_eq_one (h : n = 1) : 0 < n := by simp[h]

def isEqNat (n m : ℕ) : ℕ := if n = m then 1 else 0

def isLtNat (n m : ℕ) : ℕ := if n < m then 1 else 0

def isLeNat (n m : ℕ) : ℕ := if n ≤ m then 1 else 0

def isDvdNat (n m : ℕ) : ℕ := if n ∣ m then 1 else 0

@[simp] lemma isEqNat_pos_iff : 0 < isEqNat n m ↔ n = m := by simp[isEqNat]; by_cases n = m <;> simp[*]

@[simp] lemma isLtNat_pos_iff : 0 < isLtNat n m ↔ n < m := by simp[isLtNat]; by_cases n < m <;> simp[*]

@[simp] lemma isLeNat_pos_iff : 0 < isLeNat n m ↔ n ≤ m := by simp[isLeNat]; by_cases n ≤ m <;> simp[*]

@[simp] lemma isDvdNat_pos_iff : 0 < isDvdNat n m ↔ n ∣ m := by simp[isDvdNat]; by_cases n ∣ m <;> simp[*]

def inv (n : ℕ) : ℕ := isEqNat n 0

def pos (n : ℕ) : ℕ := isLtNat 0 n

@[simp] lemma inv_zero : inv 0 = 1 := rfl

@[simp] lemma inv_iff_ne_zero : inv n = 0 ↔ 0 < n := by simp[inv, isEqNat, zero_lt_iff]

@[simp] lemma inv_ne_zero (h : n ≠ 0) : inv n = 0 := by simp[inv, isEqNat, h]

@[simp] lemma pos_zero : pos 0 = 0 := rfl

@[simp] lemma pos_ne_zero (h : n ≠ 0) : pos n = 1 := by simp[pos, isLtNat, h]

def and (n m : ℕ) : ℕ := isLtNat 0 (n * m)

def or (n m : ℕ) : ℕ := isLtNat 0 (n + m)

lemma and_eq (n m : ℕ) : and n m = if 0 < n ∧ 0 < m then 1 else 0 := by simp [mul_pos_iff, and, isLtNat]

lemma and_eq_one (n m : ℕ) : and n m = 1 ↔ 0 < n ∧ 0 < m := by simp[and_eq, imp_false, Nat.pos_iff_ne_zero]

lemma or_eq (n m : ℕ) : or n m = if 0 < n ∨ 0 < m then 1 else 0 := by simp[or, isLtNat]

@[simp] lemma and_pos_iff (n m : ℕ) : 0 < and n m ↔ 0 < n ∧ 0 < m := by simp[and_eq]; by_cases 0 < n ∧ 0 < m <;> simp[*]

@[simp] lemma or_pos_iff (n m : ℕ) : 0 < or n m ↔ 0 < n ∨ 0 < m := by simp[or_eq]; by_cases 0 < n ∨ 0 < m <;> simp[*]

@[simp] lemma inv_pos_iff (n : ℕ) : 0 < inv n ↔ ¬0 < n := by simp[inv]

@[simp] lemma pos_pos_iff (n : ℕ) : 0 < pos n ↔ 0 < n := by simp[pos]

def ball (n : ℕ) (φ : ℕ → ℕ) : ℕ := n.rec 1 (fun n ih => (φ n).pos.and ih)

@[simp] lemma ball_pos_iff {φ : ℕ → ℕ} {n : ℕ} : 0 < ball n φ ↔ ∀ m < n, 0 < φ m := by
  induction' n with n ih <;> simp[ball, Nat.lt_succ_iff] at*
  · simp[ih]; exact ⟨
    by rintro ⟨hn, hp⟩ m hm; rcases lt_or_eq_of_le hm with (hm | rfl); { exact hp _ hm }; { exact hn },
    by intro h; exact ⟨h n (Nat.le_refl n), fun m hm => h m (le_of_lt hm)⟩⟩

@[simp] lemma ball_eq_zero_iff {φ : ℕ → ℕ} {n : ℕ} : ball n φ = 0 ↔ ∃ m < n, φ m = 0 := by
  simpa[-ball_pos_iff] using not_iff_not.mpr (ball_pos_iff (φ := φ) (n := n))

lemma ball_pos_iff_eq_one {φ : ℕ → ℕ} {n : ℕ} : ball n φ = 1 ↔ 0 < ball n φ := by
  induction' n with n _ <;> simp[ball, Nat.lt_succ_iff] at*
  · constructor
    · intro h; simpa using pos_of_eq_one h
    · intro h; simpa[and_eq_one] using h

inductive ArithPart₁ : ∀ {n}, (List.Vector ℕ n →. ℕ) → Prop
  | zero {n} : @ArithPart₁ n (fun _ => 0)
  | one {n} : @ArithPart₁ n (fun _ => 1)
  | add {n} (i j : Fin n) : @ArithPart₁ n (fun v => v.get i + v.get j : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ)
  | mul {n} (i j : Fin n) : @ArithPart₁ n (fun v => v.get i * v.get j : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ)
  | proj {n} (i : Fin n) : @ArithPart₁ n (fun v => v.get i : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ)
  | equal {n} (i j : Fin n) : @ArithPart₁ n (fun v => isEqNat (v.get i) (v.get j) : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ)
  | lt {n} (i j : Fin n) : @ArithPart₁ n (fun v => isLtNat (v.get i) (v.get j) : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ)
  | comp {m n f} (g : Fin n → List.Vector ℕ m →. ℕ) :
    ArithPart₁ f → (∀ i, ArithPart₁ (g i)) → ArithPart₁ fun v => (List.Vector.mOfFn fun i => g i v) >>= f
  | rfind {n} {f : List.Vector ℕ (n + 1) → ℕ} :
    ArithPart₁ (n := n + 1) f → ArithPart₁ (fun v => rfind fun n => Part.some (f (n ::ᵥ v) = 0))

def Arith₁ (f : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ) := ArithPart₁ (n := n) f

open Primrec

lemma to_partrec' {n} {f : List.Vector ℕ n →. ℕ} (hf : ArithPart₁ f) : Partrec' f := by
  induction hf
  case zero => exact Partrec'.of_part (Partrec.const' 0)
  case one  => exact Partrec'.of_part (Partrec.const' 1)
  case add n i j =>
    exact (Partrec'.of_part ((Primrec.nat_add.comp
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j))).to_comp.partrec))
  case mul n i j =>
    exact (Partrec'.of_part ((Primrec.nat_mul.comp
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j))).to_comp.partrec))
  case proj n i =>
    exact Partrec'.of_part
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i)).to_comp.partrec
  case equal n i j =>
    have : Primrec (fun (v : List.Vector ℕ n) => if v.get i = v.get j then 1 else 0) :=
      Primrec.ite
        (Primrec.eq.comp
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j)))
        (_root_.Primrec.const 1)
        (_root_.Primrec.const 0)
    exact Partrec'.of_part this.to_comp.partrec
  case lt n i j =>
    have : Primrec (fun (v : List.Vector ℕ n) => if v.get i < v.get j then 1 else 0) :=
      Primrec.ite
        (Primrec.nat_lt.comp
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j)))
        (_root_.Primrec.const 1)
        (_root_.Primrec.const 0)
    exact Partrec'.of_part this.to_comp.partrec
  case comp m n f g _ _ hf hg =>
    exact Partrec'.comp g hf hg
  case rfind f _ hf =>
    exact Partrec'.rfind hf

    intro v; simp

        rw[←List.Vector.mOfFn_pure]; apply congr_arg

    ArithPart₁ (fun v => Nat.rfind fun n => Part.some (f n v = 0)) := rfind h

/--
**Function extensionality** is the statement that if two functions take equal values
every point, then the functions themselves are equal: `(∀ x, f x = g x) → f = g`.
It is called "extensionality" because it talks about how to prove two objects are equal
based on the properties of the object (compare with set extensionality,
which is `(∀ x, x ∈ s ↔ x ∈ t) → s = t`).

This is often an axiom in dependent type theory systems, because it cannot be proved
from the core logic alone. However in lean's type theory this follows from the existence
of quotient types (note the `Quot.sound` in the proof, as well as the `show` line
which makes use of the definitional equality `Quot.lift f h (Quot.mk x) = f x`).
-/
theorem funext {α : Sort u} {β : α → Sort v} {f g : (x : α) → β x}
    (h : ∀ x, f x = g x) : f = g := by
  let eqv (f g : (x : α) → β x) := ∀ x, f x = g x
  let extfunApp (f : Quot eqv) (x : α) : β x :=
    Quot.liftOn f
      (fun (f : ∀ (x : α), β x) => f x)
      (fun _ _ h => h x)
  show extfunApp (Quot.mk eqv f) = extfunApp (Quot.mk eqv g)
  exact congrArg extfunApp (Quot.sound h)

/--
`List.Vector α n` is the type of lists of length `n` with elements of type `α`.

Note that there is also `Vector α n` in the root namespace,
which is the type of *arrays* of length `n` with elements of type `α`.

Typically, if you are doing programming or verification, you will primarily use `Vector α n`,
and if you are doing mathematics, you may want to use `List.Vector α n` instead.
-/
def List.Vector (α : Type u) (n : ℕ) :=
  { l : List α // l.length = n }

lemma to_partrec' {n} {f : List.Vector ℕ n →. ℕ} (hf : ArithPart₁ f) : Partrec' f := by
  induction hf
  case zero => exact Partrec'.of_part (Partrec.const' 0)
  case one  => exact Partrec'.of_part (Partrec.const' 1)
  case add n i j =>
    exact (Partrec'.of_part ((Primrec.nat_add.comp
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j))).to_comp.partrec))
  case mul n i j =>
    exact (Partrec'.of_part ((Primrec.nat_mul.comp
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j))).to_comp.partrec))
  case proj n i =>
    exact Partrec'.of_part
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i)).to_comp.partrec
  case equal n i j =>
    have : Primrec (fun (v : List.Vector ℕ n) => if v.get i = v.get j then 1 else 0) :=
      Primrec.ite
        (Primrec.eq.comp
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j)))
        (_root_.Primrec.const 1)
        (_root_.Primrec.const 0)
    exact Partrec'.of_part this.to_comp.partrec
  case lt n i j =>
    have : Primrec (fun (v : List.Vector ℕ n) => if v.get i < v.get j then 1 else 0) :=
      Primrec.ite
        (Primrec.nat_lt.comp
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j)))
        (_root_.Primrec.const 1)
        (_root_.Primrec.const 0)
    exact Partrec'.of_part this.to_comp.partrec
  case comp m n f g _ _ hf hg =>
    exact Partrec'.comp g hf hg
  case rfind f _ hf =>
    exact Partrec'.rfind hf

informal_statement: For any natural number \( n \), the vector space of \( 1 \times n \) matrices has a dimension of \( 1 \).
informal_proof:
To prove that for any natural number \( n \), the vector space of \( 1 \times n \) matrices has a dimension of \( 1 \), we proceed as follows:

1. **Understanding the Vector Space**: The vector space in question consists of all \( 1 \times n \) matrices, which can be thought of as row vectors with \( n \) entries from a given field (assumed to be the real numbers for simplicity).

2. **Definition of Dimension**: The dimension of a vector space is the number of vectors in any basis for that space.

3. **Identifying a Basis**: Consider the set containing a single vector \( \mathbf{e}_1 = [1, 0, 0, \ldots, 0] \). This vector acts as a basis for the vector space.

4. **Spanning Set**: Any \( 1 \times n \) matrix can be expressed as a scalar multiple of \( \mathbf{e}_1 \). For example, \( [a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n] = a_1 \mathbf{e}_1 + a_2 \cdot 0 + \ldots + a_n \cdot 0 \).

5. **Linear Independence**: The vector \( \mathbf{e}_1 \) is linearly independent because the only scalar multiple that results in the zero vector is the scalar \( 0 \).

6. **Uniqueness of Basis**: Since \( \mathbf{e}_1 \) spans the entire space and is linearly independent, it forms a unique basis for the vector space.

7. **Number of Basis Vectors**: There is exactly one such basis vector, hence the dimension of the vector space is \( 1 \).

8. **Conclusion**: Therefore, for any natural number \( n \), the vector space of \( 1 \times n \) matrices has a dimension of \( 1 \).

inductive ArithPart₁ : ∀ {n}, (List.Vector ℕ n →. ℕ) → Prop
  | zero {n} : @ArithPart₁ n (fun _ => 0)
  | one {n} : @ArithPart₁ n (fun _ => 1)
  | add {n} (i j : Fin n) : @ArithPart₁ n (fun v => v.get i + v.get j : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ)
  | mul {n} (i j : Fin n) : @ArithPart₁ n (fun v => v.get i * v.get j : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ)

  | comp {m n f} (g : Fin n → List.Vector ℕ m →. ℕ) :
    ArithPart₁ f → (∀ i, ArithPart₁ (g i)) → ArithPart₁ fun v => (List.Vector.mOfFn fun i => g i v) >>= f

    ArithPart₁ (n := n + 1) f → ArithPart₁ (fun v => rfind fun n => Part.some (f (n ::ᵥ v) = 0))

def Arith₁ (f : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ) := ArithPart₁ (n := n) f

lemma to_partrec' {n} {f : List.Vector ℕ n →. ℕ} (hf : ArithPart₁ f) : Partrec' f := by
  induction hf
  case zero => exact Partrec'.of_part (Partrec.const' 0)
  case one  => exact Partrec'.of_part (Partrec.const' 1)
  case add n i j =>
    exact (Partrec'.of_part ((Primrec.nat_add.comp
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j))).to_comp.partrec))
  case mul n i j =>
    exact (Partrec'.of_part ((Primrec.nat_mul.comp
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j))).to_comp.partrec))
  case proj n i =>
    exact Partrec'.of_part
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i)).to_comp.partrec
  case equal n i j =>
    have : Primrec (fun (v : List.Vector ℕ n) => if v.get i = v.get j then 1 else 0) :=
      Primrec.ite
        (Primrec.eq.comp
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j)))
        (_root_.Primrec.const 1)
        (_root_.Primrec.const 0)
    exact Partrec'.of_part this.to_comp.partrec
  case lt n i j =>
    have : Primrec (fun (v : List.Vector ℕ n) => if v.get i < v.get j then 1 else 0) :=
      Primrec.ite
        (Primrec.nat_lt.comp
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j)))
        (_root_.Primrec.const 1)
        (_root_.Primrec.const 0)
    exact Partrec'.of_part this.to_comp.partrec
  case comp m n f g _ _ hf hg =>
    exact Partrec'.comp g hf hg
  case rfind f _ hf =>
    exact Partrec'.rfind hf

lemma of_eq {n} {f g : List.Vector ℕ n →. ℕ} (hf : ArithPart₁ f) (H : ∀ i, f i = g i) : ArithPart₁ g :=
  (funext H : f = g) ▸ hf

lemma bind (f : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ →. ℕ) (hf : @ArithPart₁ (n + 1) fun v => f v.tail v.head) {g} (hg : @ArithPart₁ n g) :
    @ArithPart₁ n fun v => (g v).bind (f v) :=
  (hf.comp (g :> fun i v => v.get i) (fun i => by cases i using Fin.cases <;> simp[*]; exact proj _)).of_eq (by
    intro v; simp
    rcases Part.eq_none_or_eq_some (g v) with (hgv | ⟨x, hgv⟩)
    · simp[hgv, List.Vector.mOfFn]
    · simp[hgv, Matrix.comp_vecCons']
      have : List.Vector.mOfFn (fun i => (g :> fun j v => Part.some $ v.get j) i v) = pure (List.Vector.ofFn (x :> fun j => v.get j)) := by
        rw[←List.Vector.mOfFn_pure]; apply congr_arg
        funext i; cases i using Fin.cases <;> simp[hgv]
      simp[this])

lemma map (f : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ → ℕ) (hf : @Arith₁ (n + 1) fun v => f v.tail v.head) {g} (hg : @ArithPart₁ n g) :
    @ArithPart₁ n fun v => (g v).map (f v) :=
  (bind (Part.some $ f · ·) (hf.of_eq <| by simp) hg).of_eq <| by
  intro v; rcases Part.eq_none_or_eq_some (g v) with (_ | ⟨x, _⟩) <;> simp[*]

lemma comp₁ (f : ℕ →. ℕ) (hf : @ArithPart₁ 1 fun v => f (v.get 0)) {n g} (hg : @Arith₁ n g) :
    @ArithPart₁ n fun v => f (g v) :=
  (hf.comp _ fun _ => hg).of_eq (by simp)

lemma comp₂ (f : ℕ → ℕ →. ℕ) (hf : @ArithPart₁ 2 fun v => f (v.get 0) (v.get 1)) {n g h} (hg : @Arith₁ n g) (hh : @Arith₁ n h) :
    @ArithPart₁ n fun v => f (g v) (h v) :=
  (hf.comp ![g, h] (fun i => i.cases hg (fun i => by simpa using hh))).of_eq
    (by intro i
        have : (fun j => (![↑g, h] : Fin 2 → List.Vector ℕ n →. ℕ) j i) = (fun j => pure (![g i, h i] j)) := by
          funext j; cases j using Fin.cases <;> simp[Fin.eq_zero]
        simp[Matrix.comp_vecCons']; simp[this] )

lemma to_partrec' {n} {f : List.Vector ℕ n →. ℕ} (hf : ArithPart₁ f) : Partrec' f := by
  induction hf
  case zero => exact Partrec'.of_part (Partrec.const' 0)
  case one  => exact Partrec'.of_part (Partrec.const' 1)
  case add n i j =>
    exact (Partrec'.of_part ((Primrec.nat_add.comp
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j))).to_comp.partrec))
  case mul n i j =>
    exact (Partrec'.of_part ((Primrec.nat_mul.comp
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j))).to_comp.partrec))
  case proj n i =>
    exact Partrec'.of_part
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i)).to_comp.partrec
  case equal n i j =>
    have : Primrec (fun (v : List.Vector ℕ n) => if v.get i = v.get j then 1 else 0) :=
      Primrec.ite
        (Primrec.eq.comp
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j)))
        (_root_.Primrec.const 1)
        (_root_.Primrec.const 0)
    exact Partrec'.of_part this.to_comp.partrec
  case lt n i j =>
    have : Primrec (fun (v : List.Vector ℕ n) => if v.get i < v.get j then 1 else 0) :=
      Primrec.ite
        (Primrec.nat_lt.comp
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j)))
        (_root_.Primrec.const 1)
        (_root_.Primrec.const 0)
    exact Partrec'.of_part this.to_comp.partrec
  case comp m n f g _ _ hf hg =>
    exact Partrec'.comp g hf hg
  case rfind f _ hf =>
    exact Partrec'.rfind hf

    intro v; simp
    rcases Part.eq_none_or_eq_some (g v) with (hgv | ⟨x, hgv⟩)

        rw[←List.Vector.mOfFn_pure]; apply congr_arg
        funext i; cases i using Fin.cases <;> simp[hgv]
      simp[this])

/--
`List.Vector α n` is the type of lists of length `n` with elements of type `α`.

Note that there is also `Vector α n` in the root namespace,
which is the type of *arrays* of length `n` with elements of type `α`.

Typically, if you are doing programming or verification, you will primarily use `Vector α n`,
and if you are doing mathematics, you may want to use `List.Vector α n` instead.

def List.Vector (α : Type u) (n : ℕ) :=
  { l : List α // l.length = n }

Note that there is also `Vector α n` in the root namespace,
which is the type of *arrays* of length `n` with elements of type `α`.

Typically, if you are doing programming or verification, you will primarily use `Vector α n`,
and if you are doing mathematics, you may want to use `List.Vector α n` instead.
-/
def List.Vector (α : Type u) (n : ℕ) :=
  { l : List α // l.length = n }

lemma pos_of_eq_one (h : n = 1) : 0 < n := by simp[h]

def isEqNat (n m : ℕ) : ℕ := if n = m then 1 else 0

def isLtNat (n m : ℕ) : ℕ := if n < m then 1 else 0

def isLeNat (n m : ℕ) : ℕ := if n ≤ m then 1 else 0

def isDvdNat (n m : ℕ) : ℕ := if n ∣ m then 1 else 0

@[simp] lemma isEqNat_pos_iff : 0 < isEqNat n m ↔ n = m := by simp[isEqNat]; by_cases n = m <;> simp[*]

@[simp] lemma isLtNat_pos_iff : 0 < isLtNat n m ↔ n < m := by simp[isLtNat]; by_cases n < m <;> simp[*]

@[simp] lemma isLeNat_pos_iff : 0 < isLeNat n m ↔ n ≤ m := by simp[isLeNat]; by_cases n ≤ m <;> simp[*]

@[simp] lemma isDvdNat_pos_iff : 0 < isDvdNat n m ↔ n ∣ m := by simp[isDvdNat]; by_cases n ∣ m <;> simp[*]

def inv (n : ℕ) : ℕ := isEqNat n 0

def pos (n : ℕ) : ℕ := isLtNat 0 n

@[simp] lemma inv_zero : inv 0 = 1 := rfl

@[simp] lemma inv_iff_ne_zero : inv n = 0 ↔ 0 < n := by simp[inv, isEqNat, zero_lt_iff]

@[simp] lemma inv_ne_zero (h : n ≠ 0) : inv n = 0 := by simp[inv, isEqNat, h]

@[simp] lemma pos_zero : pos 0 = 0 := rfl

@[simp] lemma pos_ne_zero (h : n ≠ 0) : pos n = 1 := by simp[pos, isLtNat, h]

def and (n m : ℕ) : ℕ := isLtNat 0 (n * m)

def or (n m : ℕ) : ℕ := isLtNat 0 (n + m)

lemma and_eq (n m : ℕ) : and n m = if 0 < n ∧ 0 < m then 1 else 0 := by simp [mul_pos_iff, and, isLtNat]

lemma and_eq_one (n m : ℕ) : and n m = 1 ↔ 0 < n ∧ 0 < m := by simp[and_eq, imp_false, Nat.pos_iff_ne_zero]

lemma or_eq (n m : ℕ) : or n m = if 0 < n ∨ 0 < m then 1 else 0 := by simp[or, isLtNat]

@[simp] lemma and_pos_iff (n m : ℕ) : 0 < and n m ↔ 0 < n ∧ 0 < m := by simp[and_eq]; by_cases 0 < n ∧ 0 < m <;> simp[*]

@[simp] lemma or_pos_iff (n m : ℕ) : 0 < or n m ↔ 0 < n ∨ 0 < m := by simp[or_eq]; by_cases 0 < n ∨ 0 < m <;> simp[*]

@[simp] lemma inv_pos_iff (n : ℕ) : 0 < inv n ↔ ¬0 < n := by simp[inv]

@[simp] lemma pos_pos_iff (n : ℕ) : 0 < pos n ↔ 0 < n := by simp[pos]

def ball (n : ℕ) (φ : ℕ → ℕ) : ℕ := n.rec 1 (fun n ih => (φ n).pos.and ih)

@[simp] lemma ball_pos_iff {φ : ℕ → ℕ} {n : ℕ} : 0 < ball n φ ↔ ∀ m < n, 0 < φ m := by
  induction' n with n ih <;> simp[ball, Nat.lt_succ_iff] at*
  · simp[ih]; exact ⟨
    by rintro ⟨hn, hp⟩ m hm; rcases lt_or_eq_of_le hm with (hm | rfl); { exact hp _ hm }; { exact hn },
    by intro h; exact ⟨h n (Nat.le_refl n), fun m hm => h m (le_of_lt hm)⟩⟩

@[simp] lemma ball_eq_zero_iff {φ : ℕ → ℕ} {n : ℕ} : ball n φ = 0 ↔ ∃ m < n, φ m = 0 := by
  simpa[-ball_pos_iff] using not_iff_not.mpr (ball_pos_iff (φ := φ) (n := n))

  · constructor
    · intro h; simpa using pos_of_eq_one h
    · intro h; simpa[and_eq_one] using h

inductive ArithPart₁ : ∀ {n}, (List.Vector ℕ n →. ℕ) → Prop
  | zero {n} : @ArithPart₁ n (fun _ => 0)
  | one {n} : @ArithPart₁ n (fun _ => 1)
  | add {n} (i j : Fin n) : @ArithPart₁ n (fun v => v.get i + v.get j : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ)
  | mul {n} (i j : Fin n) : @ArithPart₁ n (fun v => v.get i * v.get j : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ)
  | proj {n} (i : Fin n) : @ArithPart₁ n (fun v => v.get i : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ)
  | equal {n} (i j : Fin n) : @ArithPart₁ n (fun v => isEqNat (v.get i) (v.get j) : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ)
  | lt {n} (i j : Fin n) : @ArithPart₁ n (fun v => isLtNat (v.get i) (v.get j) : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ)
  | comp {m n f} (g : Fin n → List.Vector ℕ m →. ℕ) :
    ArithPart₁ f → (∀ i, ArithPart₁ (g i)) → ArithPart₁ fun v => (List.Vector.mOfFn fun i => g i v) >>= f
  | rfind {n} {f : List.Vector ℕ (n + 1) → ℕ} :
    ArithPart₁ (n := n + 1) f → ArithPart₁ (fun v => rfind fun n => Part.some (f (n ::ᵥ v) = 0))

def Arith₁ (f : List.Vector ℕ n → ℕ) := ArithPart₁ (n := n) f

lemma to_partrec' {n} {f : List.Vector ℕ n →. ℕ} (hf : ArithPart₁ f) : Partrec' f := by
  induction hf
  case zero => exact Partrec'.of_part (Partrec.const' 0)
  case one  => exact Partrec'.of_part (Partrec.const' 1)
  case add n i j =>
    exact (Partrec'.of_part ((Primrec.nat_add.comp
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j))).to_comp.partrec))
  case mul n i j =>
    exact (Partrec'.of_part ((Primrec.nat_mul.comp
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j))).to_comp.partrec))
  case proj n i =>
    exact Partrec'.of_part
      (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i)).to_comp.partrec
  case equal n i j =>
    have : Primrec (fun (v : List.Vector ℕ n) => if v.get i = v.get j then 1 else 0) :=
      Primrec.ite
        (Primrec.eq.comp
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j)))
        (_root_.Primrec.const 1)
        (_root_.Primrec.const 0)
    exact Partrec'.of_part this.to_comp.partrec
  case lt n i j =>
    have : Primrec (fun (v : List.Vector ℕ n) => if v.get i < v.get j then 1 else 0) :=
      Primrec.ite
        (Primrec.nat_lt.comp
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const i))
          (Primrec.vector_get.comp _root_.Primrec.id (_root_.Primrec.const j)))
        (_root_.Primrec.const 1)
        (_root_.Primrec.const 0)
    exact Partrec'.of_part this.to_comp.partrec
  case comp m n f g _ _ hf hg =>
    exact Partrec'.comp g hf hg
  case rfind f _ hf =>
    exact Partrec'.rfind hf
